question: Can frozen camera slots replace engineered object tracks for offline Genesis prediction?
hypothesis: Temporal slots can supply sufficiently persistent object observations for M5 or a matched S1 predictor, without labels in representation or dynamics training.

sources.sections: Sections 3.1-3.3, temporal recurrence; Appendices C.1, C.5, C.6
sources.consequence: Carry slots across every frame; learned grouping is not a guarantee of stable physical identity, so measure switches and fragmentation.
Use frozen DINO features and slot encoder; distinguish predictive object state from causal-mechanism identification.

differences: Use existing local s0 unchanged, with DINOv2 cached features and range-assisted positions. Six slots, real simulator pose/full layout, previously used validation corpus. Our world-position adapter and visibility/track metrics are local engineering extensions, not claims reproduced from VideoSAUR.
contrary_evidence: Binding at one frame does not establish identity continuity; missing objects can make conditional error look good. Full map and true pose simplify localization. A predictor trained on engineered tracks can fail under slot observation noise even when slots identify walkers.

tracks.positions: mask column bearing, nearest valid range plus walker radius, exclude walls

protocol.evaluation: Same 100 units and same matched initially-in-view cases. Preserve legacy visible-at-target summary and add initially-visible after-occlusion cohort. Report found share and precision, ID switches, fragmentation, missing prediction coverage, p50/p90/p95 at 1.6/3.2/6.4s and waiting subset; arms compared on intersection with coverage reported.
checks: old M5 summary unchanged with default adapter
no walker labels in tracks or S1 targets

success: Slot found share >=0.9 of tracker on same in-view frames; better of M5/S1 median3.2s <=1.5x engineered M5, both reported; beat slot CV at3.2s and6.4s.
stop: Do not run Genesis missions or collect new data. Missing coverage or failed gate must be reported, not hidden through matching. No s0 retraining.
